facts.text: Darnestown Heritage Park, a 0.6‑acre county park, serves as an outdoor museum with markers that chronicle the town’s history.
The Chesapeake & Ohio Canal’s lock house and Riley’s Lock are part of the national park and are toured by local Girl Scouts each spring and fall.
Andrew Small, a Scottish benefactor who worked on the C & O Canal, gave his name to the largest school building in Montgomery County at the time.
The ancient Seneca Indian Trail, once a major route for Indigenous peoples, runs through Darnestown and is still visible in the landscape.
Darnestown’s growth in the 19th century was fueled by the Chesapeake & Ohio Canal, which spurred local gristmills and other industries.
Reed Brothers Dodge, a family‑owned dealership founded in 1915, mirrors nearly a century of American automobile history right in Darnestown.
